title: "form owner" definition seems very obtuse
body:
https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/form-control-infrastructure.html#form-owner

As far as I can tell all of the association/reset stuff could be replaced with an algorithm to determine the current form owner. The algorithm would probably look a lot like the the current one for "reset the form owner", or like https://github.com/jsdom/jsdom/blob/a70e1ae4fca8f596863e4fae5df932bd38809cf7/lib/jsdom/living/helpers/form-controls.js#L219 .

However, the Blink source code seems to implement all of the spec's complexity. So I suspect I am missing something. I [tried the semi-complicated example in the spec](http://software.hixie.ch/utilities/js/live-dom-viewer/?saved=6240), but as far as I can tell the simple algorithm (i.e. form owner = `closest("form")`) still works in that snippet.

One hint might be found in this note:

> They are also complicated by rules in the HTML parser that, for historical reasons, can result in a form-associated element being associated with a form element that is not its ancestor.

which is probably referring to [this part of the parser](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/parsing.html#creating-and-inserting-nodes:concept-form-association). But maybe even then, we could have a simple algorithm which also consults a "parser-override form owner"?

/cc @smaug---- and @tkent-google for help.

I hope we can resolve this issue by either drastically simplifying the spec, or (more likely) adding explanatory text and examples as to why it is the complicated way that it currently is.
